The generic catalog test (`test_invocation_view_catalog_exercises_span_hierarchy_assertions` in `tests/test_resources.py`) only validates the shape of `links` (item count and attribute-key presence), not which specific selector carries the two-item continuation pattern. It passes identically whether this `$occurrence` link sits on the `otel-condition` (SUCCEEDED) selector, as fixed here, or on `otel-condition attempt 1`, as it incorrectly did before this PR. That means this exact bug class — placing the continuation link on the wrong operation-lifecycle span — can regress or reoccur in another case without CI catching it.

Consider adding a targeted assertion (e.g. alongside `test_invocation_view_catalog_exercises_span_hierarchy_assertions`, or a dedicated case-9 test) that pins the continuation link to the selector whose `parent` resolves to `Invocation`/`Workflow` rather than to the initial operation span, mirroring the already-consistent placement in `otel-invocation-2` (`otel-wait`) and `otel-invocation-3` (`otel-retry`).
